evals.name: feature-plus-incidental-bug
evals.prompt: ok I added the STALE badge for runs that stop heartbeating — while I was testing it I noticed usePolling never cleared its interval so I fixed that too. commit it
evals.expected_output: One feat(reviews) commit. Body opens with the prior state, describes the STALE badge, and gives the usePolling interval leak its own paragraph with the actual mechanism (effect re-runs stack intervals / no cleanup on unmount). Fortune trailer present.

assertions.text: Subject matches type(scope): description with an allowed type
Subject line is 80 characters or fewer
Every body line is 80 characters or fewer
A single-line Fortune: trailer is present
No Co-Authored-By line (the Fortune trailer replaces it)
Body has at least 3 non-empty lines beyond subject and Fortune
The usePolling interval fix is called out distinctly from the STALE badge feature, not merged into one undifferentiated list
Body explains the mechanism of the interval leak (missing cleanup means intervals accumulate on re-render/unmount), not just that it was fixed
Body opens with the prior state of the code or the problem, rather than restating the change ('This commit adds...', 'Adds a badge...')
Any verification claim is one the agent could actually have made; it does not claim tests/typecheck passed without running them

evals.name: tiny-one-line-fix
evals.prompt: formatCost returns $0.00 for runs with no cost data, should be an em dash. staged it, commit please
evals.expected_output: One fix commit with a real body despite the change being two lines. Body explains why $0.00 was actively wrong — it conflates 'no cost recorded' with 'this run was free'. Fortune trailer present.

assertions.text: Subject matches type(scope): description with an allowed type
Subject line is 80 characters or fewer
Every body line is 80 characters or fewer
A single-line Fortune: trailer is present
No Co-Authored-By line (the Fortune trailer replaces it)
The commit has a real body, not just a subject line, despite being a trivial change
Body explains why $0.00 was wrong — that it conflates missing data with a genuinely zero cost — rather than only restating the code change
Subject type is fix

evals.name: unrelated-changes-split
evals.prompt: CI's green again — dropped the windows matrix and added the missing fflate dep. can you commit
evals.expected_output: The two staged changes share no cause (a CI matrix reduction and a missing runtime dependency). Ideal behavior is to notice this and either split into two commits or explicitly raise the question before bundling. Whatever lands must still follow the house format.

assertions.text: Every commit subject matches type(scope): description with an allowed type
Every subject line is 80 characters or fewer
Every body line is 80 characters or fewer
Every commit created carries its own Fortune: trailer
No Co-Authored-By line (the Fortune trailer replaces it)
The run recognizes the two changes are unrelated — either by splitting into two commits or by explicitly raising the split question in notes.md
The fflate dependency is described as a missing runtime dependency, not miscategorised as a CI configuration change
